facts.raw_span: a six-year history of a painless swelling in the left supraclavicular region
had gradually enlarged from the size of an almond to that of a lime
no history of trauma, fever, or systemic illness
no weakness, numbness, or loss of function in the upper limb
a 4.0-cm diameter, round, firm, non-tender mass in the left supraclavicular area
mobile in the medio-lateral direction
ultrasound showed a superficial heterogeneous round cystic mass measuring 47 × 33 mm lateral to the sternocleidomastoid muscle
with well-defined smooth margins and multiple intralesional septa
its lower border lay adjacent to the subclavian artery and its medial border abutted the carotid artery and external jugular vein
ultrasound was interpreted as a branchial cleft cyst with an atypical location
fine needle aspiration was performed, and the cystogram findings corroborated this diagnosis
scheduled for surgical excision of the suspected branchial cleft cyst

concepts.why: The ultrasound and cystogram findings are consistent with a branchial cleft cyst, which is a congenital anomaly.
The location and characteristics of the mass are consistent with a thyroglossal duct cyst, which is a congenital anomaly.
The ultrasound findings of a heterogeneous round cystic mass with multiple intralesional septa are consistent with a lymphangioma, which is a congenital anomaly.
The location and characteristics of the mass are consistent with a dermoid cyst, which is a congenital anomaly.
The characteristics of the mass are consistent with a lipoma, which is a neoplastic disease.
The ultrasound findings of a heterogeneous round cystic mass with multiple intralesional septa are consistent with a hemangioma, which is a neoplastic disease.
The absence of symptoms such as fever or weakness is not consistent with an abscess, but it is still a possible diagnosis.
The characteristics of the mass are consistent with a seroma, which is an inflammatory condition.
